idiom_name: immutable data classes + top-level `fun XRow.toDomain()` mappers in the infrastructure module
implementation_notes: Kotlin expresses the domain model as immutable data classes whose init/require blocks guard invariants and whose transitions return copies; what replaces the Mapper class is a set of top-level extension functions in the infrastructure module (fun OrderEntity.toDomain(): Order, fun Order.toEntity(): OrderEntity), so the mapping reads as ordinary code and the domain module imports nothing from Exposed, JPA or kotlinx.serialization. Exposed's table objects or JPA entity classes stay infrastructure-side, and JPA in particular must not be mapped onto data classes - they are final, have an invariant-defining constructor and generate equals/hashCode/copy over all properties, all of which conflict with Hibernate's identity, proxy and dirty-tracking model.
pitfalls: data class + JPA: Hibernate needs open classes, a no-arg constructor and mutable fields, while generated equals/hashCode over all properties corrupts Set/Map membership for managed entities and copy() produces detached duplicates.
Serialization annotations on domain types (@Serializable, @JsonIgnore) put the transport contract into the model - keep them on DTO/entity classes and map explicitly.

Extension-function mappers are invisible dependencies: nothing forces the infra module to be the only caller, so a domain class can still acquire a toEntity() extension next to it unless the module boundary is enforced by the build.
